newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money rates stable, downward pressure noted.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money rates stable, downward pressure noted.

text.p: Dutch money rates were stable on Wednesday, but dealers said there was some downward pressure on the market with several foreign players turning to the Netherlands and Germany due to EMU uncertainty.
"It is mainly foreign participants that are offering money," said one dealer, adding domestic investors were more likely to step into the share market with its higher returns.
Another dealer said foreign investors were fleeing into 'safe currencies', like the Dutch guilder and the mark, leading to more offerings on these money markets.
"Investors will turn away from European countries with weaker currencies as long as the EMU uncertainty continues," said one dealer.
Another dealer said some swap business had been done with marks and U.S. dollars.
"But, there is hardly any offering from domestic investors,' said another dealer.
Dealers expect the Dutch special advances rate would remain 2.90 percent when the central bank sets a new pact this afternoon at 1400 GMT.
"The guilder is stable versus the mark and the current rate for deposits does not demand an easing of the advances rate," said one dealer.

He added there was some speculation in the market that Germany could lower its repo rate (comparable to the Dutch special advances rate) by 10 basis points to 2.90 percent in the near future. The Bundesbank left rates unchanged today.
"German money market rates have been fairly low recently, lower than the Dutch," he said.
He added any delay in the introduction of the Euro would certainly press German rates lower.
Dutch call money was bid at an unchanged 3.00 percent and three-month deposits were stable at 3.18 percent bid.
The guilder was steady at 112.495 per 100 marks against 112.50 on Wednesday.
